output.summary: KEP-3327 adds a new CPUManager static-policy option, `align-by-socket`, so that CPUs on a socket are treated as aligned and the CPUManager sends socket-aligned preferred hints to the TopologyManager. Status is implementable, stage alpha.
output.rationale: On CPUs with several NUMA nodes per socket, the CPUs per NUMA node shrink, so perfect NUMA alignment with devices is hard to reach. The default CPUManager prefers the minimum NUMA-node count, which can span sockets and degrade performance. Widening the alignment scope to the socket boundary gives the TopologyManager more socket-aligned hints to choose from.

alternatives.option: Introduce align-by-socket as a TopologyManager policy
alternatives.why_not: The TopologyManager's function is to act as arbitrator for hint providers and should decide based on the hints provided, not influence BestHint with its own policy.

alternatives.option: Support systems with multiple sockets per NUMA node by allowing alignment across sockets
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers asked for this to be handled; the author leaned toward erroring out when there is more than one socket per NUMA node, since such machines are rare. The sources do not record a final resolution beyond this lean.

evidence.quote: With this policy option CPUs will be considered aligned at socket boundary instead of NUMA boundary during allocation.
However, if the NUMA nodes selected for allocation are spread across sockets, it results in degraded performance.
Updated the KEP, i am leaning towards erring out in case there are more than one socket per NUMA
Agreed with @klueska above at: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3334#issuecomment-1161476253 Added some comments as the non blocker for alpha too.
